name: No rugs: four-screen run as the anchor, a lamp at each station, art over the chair bed
notes:
Rug-free (F-66): the staged arrangement (a) with the LOHALS flatweave taken out; every other piece stands where it does in a, plus one desk lamp. rug-2, the Anji Mountain bamboo chair mat (48 x 42", rug layer, x 33.75-75.75, y 40.75-88.75), lies under chair-1 at the personal run in place of the clear plastic KOLON (Andrew, 2026-10-25: "something that isn't literally plastic"): bamboo on a felt back, wipeable and plastic-free (F-66), and it keeps the casters off the floor. If the floor turns out to be wood, a second one under chair-2 at the work desk would protect it.
What ties the room together instead:
(1) The anchor is the personal run: the two white MITTZONs end to end along the right wall (102 3/8"), with the work desk and the chair bed facing it across the room.
(2) A lamp for each zone the rug's aisle used to join: a new RÖDFLIK on the run's window-end front corner, the RÖDFLIK on the work desk, the RÖDFLIK on the BESTÅ as the chair bed's reading lamp, and the TÅGARP uplighter in the bottom-left corner for the whole room. No second floor lamp fits without narrowing the 41.4" walkway or standing where the opened chair bed goes.
(3) The wall anchor is the PJÄTTERYD set, three 22" canvases (68") on the left wall over the BESTÅ and the chair bed, which the run faces when you turn around. No art hangs over the run itself, where the four screens cover the wall.
(4) The rug's natural tone moves up into the sand of the PJÄTTERYD and the TRAVSPORT's oak effect; the gray-green repeats in the VALLKRASSING cushion, the guest's ÄNGSLILJA duvet cover, the FREIVID mat and the monstera; the white of the desks, the BESTÅ and the HOPPVALS blinds ties the rest. Every textile here is washable, and the FREIVID's cover goes in the machine.
(5) The FEJKA monstera stands by the wardrobe. An artificial plant gathers dust, so it is wiped with the dusting.
Clearances are as in a (F-31, F-32, F-33, F-35, F-62). The usable floor runs from y 12 (furniture) and y 18 (upholstery) off the heater wall to y 116 at the wardrobe's landing and y 122 at the door's. desk-1 is 7.6" from the heater face. desk-3 is 6" from it, with 47" behind it. The personal run has 47" to the work desk. storage-1 has 29.5" in front of its door. The chair bed is 1.6" above the wardrobe's landing, with a 41.4" walkway between it and desk-2 (assumed-position:door, assumed-position:closet, heater-depth-assumed).
Audit 2026-10-24: the plan stands, with two notes added. The work desk's window end is 12" from the window wall and chair-2 beside it rolls, so Maddie could climb to the window: fit window stops or guards there (not in the catalog; the sill is unmeasured, F-38). Opened, the chair bed's foot goes under desk-2, so nothing stands under that desk (a PC tower goes under desk-1), and desk-2 stays raised and unplugged while a guest sleeps, so nobody lowers it onto the bed.
2026-10-25: the KOLON ($24.99) gave way to the bamboo mat ($111.59). Total $3,024.35, prices as of 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-25 (those before today are price-stale, F-02).
